text: Everything built so far exists to support about two minutes of conversation on Monday. That conversation is where this project actually lands or doesn't — so this lesson is entirely about how to run it.

The biggest mistake is walking through the dashboard visual by visual, top to bottom, narrating what each one is before saying what it means. For someone glancing at this before a call, that's backwards. Lead with the answer to their actual question, stated in one sentence, before pointing at anything on screen.

A simple structure covers it. First, the headline — ten to fifteen seconds, the KPI cards turned into a sentence, not just pointed at. Second, the why — thirty to forty five seconds on the bar chart, showing what's actually driving that headline number. Third, the detail table — but only if the conversation calls for it, not narrated by default.

Something like this, said out loud before touching anything: overall, this quarter is up compared to last, total sales are this much, across this many orders, and the Southeast is tracking with the rest of the territories. That's the headline, stated plainly, first.

And use the slicer live, not just as a line in your explanation — click the Southeast territory in front of the stakeholder and let them watch the cards and chart update. Seeing it respond lands better than being told it can. When a question comes up the report wasn't built to answer, like a year over year comparison, say so plainly: not in this version, happy to add it as a follow up. That protects your credibility and turns a gap into the start of the next iteration.
That's how you present this dashboard well. Last lesson of this project: a recap of everything you actually built, and a look at where the Intermediate project picks up from here.
